assets.agent:files/hermes-launcher.sh:
#!/bin/sh
# Managed by the workstation engine — the agent package's hermes launcher.
#
# The engine provisions the full stack: the pinned interpreter at
# .local/opt/hermes/python (download contract, checksum-gated archive) and
# the pinned checkout at .hermes/hermes-agent (git recipe). This launcher
# resolves both at run time (never baked paths), so the bytes stay
# machine-independent. A missing or non-executable interpreter or checkout
# fails closed: the verify lane asserts this exact smoke.
set -eu

checkout=${HERMES_ENGINE_CHECKOUT:-$HOME/.hermes/hermes-agent}
python=$HOME/.local/opt/hermes/python/bin/python3

if [ ! -x "$python" ]; then
  echo "hermes: pinned interpreter missing at $python (run: workstation apply)" >&2
  exit 2
fi
if [ ! -f "$checkout/hermes_cli/main.py" ]; then
  echo "hermes: pinned checkout missing at $checkout (run: workstation apply)" >&2
  exit 2
fi

HERMES_ENGINE_CHECKOUT=$checkout
export HERMES_ENGINE_CHECKOUT
# Same posture as upstream's launcher: isolated interpreter, no inherited
# PYTHON* config, bytecode kept out of the engine-owned checkout.
PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX=${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/hermes-pycache
export PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX

exec "$python" -I -c 'import os, sys
os.environ.pop("PYTHONHOME", None)
os.environ.pop("PYTHONPATH", None)
sys.path.insert(0, os.environ["HERMES_ENGINE_CHECKOUT"])
import hermes_bootstrap
from hermes_cli.main import main
sys.exit(main())' "$@"
assets.foundation:files/mise.sh:
# Managed by chezmoi. Activate the engine-managed mise in shells that have
# an activate hook (bash, zsh); plain sh has no activate variant, so it
# stays a no-op there — version resolution rides the engine's managed
# config and each project's .tool-versions either way.
#
# The engine owns the mise footprint end to end: the pinned binary lives
# in the engine's opt root (.local/opt/mise/<version>/bin/mise) and the
# engine's apply keeps the ~/.local/bin/mise symlink aimed at the current
# pin. This fragment activates THE ENGINE'S BINARY by absolute path and
# never a bare `mise` from PATH: PATH resolution binds whatever mise ranks
# first (on a host with a distro mise under /usr/bin that is never the
# engine's), and a foreign mise version paired with the engine's managed
# data and config split-brains every project tool resolution (the
# 2026-10-20 omarchy failure). Resolution order: the engine launcher
# symlink — honored only in its contract shape (../opt/mise/<version>/
# bin/mise), so a stray or foreign link is refused — else the sole
# opt-root pin (found with find, so zsh never trips an unmatched glob);
# anything else — an ambiguous multi-pin tree, an absent tree, a foreign
# file at the launcher path — activates nothing, because the engine's
# data and config are never handed to a non-engine mise. Both variables
# are mise-namespaced, so nothing outside mise sees them.
mise_engine_bin=
if [ -L "$HOME/.local/bin/mise" ]; then
  mise_link=$(readlink "$HOME/.local/bin/mise" 2>/dev/null || true)
  case $mise_link in
    ../opt/mise/*/bin/mise)
      mise_version=${mise_link#../opt/mise/}
      mise_version=${mise_version%/bin/mise}
      mise_engine_bin=$HOME/.local/opt/mise/$mise_version/bin/mise
      ;;
  esac
fi
if [ ! -x "$mise_engine_bin" ]; then
  mise_engine_bin=$(
    find "$HOME/.local/opt/mise" -type f -path '*/bin/mise' -perm -u+x 2>/dev/null |
      head -n 2
  )
  case $mise_engine_bin in
    # exactly one pin: keep it; none, or several (a superseded pin's tree
    # still on disk): refuse rather than guess
    '' | *'
'*) mise_engine_bin= ;;
  esac
fi
if [ -n "$mise_engine_bin" ]; then
  MISE_DATA_DIR="$HOME/.local/state/workstation/mise"
  MISE_CONFIG_DIR="$HOME/.config/mise"
  export MISE_DATA_DIR MISE_CONFIG_DIR
  if [ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
    eval "$("$mise_engine_bin" activate zsh)"
  elif [ -n "${BASH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
    eval "$("$mise_engine_bin" activate bash)"
  fi
fi
unset mise_engine_bin mise_link mise_version
assets.tmux:files/.tmux.conf:
# Keep terminal input responsive inside Neovim and other interactive programs.
set -sg escape-time 10

# Pass focus changes through to applications running inside tmux.
set -g focus-events on

# Enable mouse selection, scrolling, pane selection, and resizing.
set -g mouse on

# Mobile-client redraw mitigation (aurora, 2026-10-13): keep tmux's
# clear-scrolls-history repaint off so full-screen clears repaint in place —
# scroll-style output is what limited mobile clients (Termius/iOS) render as
# stacked lines. Version-guarded so releases without the option (pre-3.4)
# still parse; an unknown option at parse time would fail the whole
# .tmux.conf.
%if "#{>=:#{version},3.5}"
set -g scroll-on-clear off
%endif

# Keep the status bar at tmux's traditional bottom edge, even after sourcing
# desktop/distribution configs that moved it.
set -g status-position bottom

# Advertise modern color support inside tmux.
set -g default-terminal "tmux-256color"
set -s terminal-features[100] "xterm-256color:RGB"

# TPM loads whatever's on disk at ~/.tmux/plugins/<name>. Every checkout is
# engine-provisioned as a pinned-clone recipe (exact commit, idempotent
# apply — never placed by hand): the nunchux checkout by its own package,
# the TPM plugin set by the tmux package's git recipes (docs/tmux.md). TPM
# sees the pre-installed checkouts and sources them without cloning; its
# '#<ref>' syntax only accepts branches/tags, not SHAs, which is why the
# pins live in the recipes.
set -g @plugin 'tmux-plugins/tpm'
set -g @plugin '2KAbhishek/tmux2k'
set -g @plugin 'tmux-plugins/tmux-yank'
set -g @plugin 'christoomey/vim-tmux-navigator'
set -g @plugin 'tmux-plugins/tmux-resurrect'
# nunchux: the checkout is engine-provisioned by the package's pinned-clone
# recipe (Workstation.Packages.Nunchux; docs/tmux.md) — the plugin source
# below rides that checkout, and the root chord matches @nunchux-key.
set -g @plugin 'datamadsen/nunchux'
# The nunchux key is declared ahead of TPM init. Upstream binds keys
# containing "-" without a prefix, so this is the root C-g chord. Rebound
# off upstream's default C-Space (operator directive, 2026-10-21): tmux's
# root C-Space claim intercepted the chord ahead of nvim, killing blink.cmp's
# insert-mode completion trigger (the LazyVim blink extra binds <C-space> to
# show completion — presets.lua "enter" preset). C-g is free on both
# surfaces — no tmux plugin here binds it, and nvim uses it only for
# obscure builtins (:file info; a rare insert cursor-motion prefix) — while
# keeping the no-prefix single-chord shape (upstream itself names C-g as
# the canonical root "-" key beside C-Space).
set -g @nunchux-key 'C-g'
# Root-chord popup, exactly as nunchux.tmux builds it (60%/50% are upstream's
# menu_width/menu_height defaults); declared here so the chord is ours to
# revert in one line (comment this bind and re-apply).
bind -n C-g display-popup -E -B -d '#{pane_current_path}' -w '60%' -h '50%' '~/.tmux/plugins/nunchux/bin/nunchux'

# Keep Ctrl-h/j/k/l navigation inside a zoomed Neovim pane.
set -g @tmux_navigator_disable_when_zoomed '1'

# Cycle windows using Shift + Arrow keys (No prefix needed)
bind -n S-Left previous-window
bind -n S-Right next-window

# tmux2k status bar — onedark theme, cpu/ram on the right; clicking cpu/ram
# opens btop (mise-managed on every host via the engine's mise contract).
# Window highlighting is TEXT-ONLY (operator decision, 2026-10-14): the
# active window renders onedark blue text, inactive windows onedark comment
# gray, both on the terminal's own background — no window pills. Mechanics:
# tmux2k resolves colors through variable indirection (${!colors[i]}), so
# `dark_blue` pinned to the literal `default` makes the window background
# slots `bg=default`; the powerline separators stay on for the module
# segments but the WINDOW separator glyphs are emptied (a styled span with
# zero characters paints nothing). Module segments keep upstream onedark
# powerline pills verbatim — no color overrides.
set -g @tmux2k-theme 'onedark'
set -g @tmux2k-bg-main 'default'
set -g @tmux2k-bg-alt 'default'
set -g @tmux2k-dark-blue 'default'
set -g @tmux2k-white '#5c6370'
set -g @tmux2k-window-list-colors 'blue dark_blue'
set -g @tmux2k-window-list-left-sep ''
set -g @tmux2k-window-list-right-sep ''
set -g @tmux2k-right-plugins 'cpu ram time'
set -g @tmux2k-ram-popup-cmd 'btop'
set -g @tmux2k-time-format '%a %H:%M'

# TPM redirects its plugin root to ~/.config/tmux/plugins whenever an XDG
# ~/.config/tmux/tmux.conf exists; the managed XDG symlink above would trip
# that, and TPM then silently sources nothing. Pin the managed plugin root.
set-environment -g TMUX_PLUGIN_MANAGER_PATH '~/.tmux/plugins/'

# Initialize TPM after every plugin and plugin option has been declared.
run-shell '~/.tmux/plugins/tpm/tpm'
